prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures an egocentric view of the camera wearer looking upward and forward at an exposed metal-stud wall and soffit structure on a deck, with no other people present in the scene. The wearer's right arm and C-clamp in the lower-right foreground are brightest at roughly 0.2 to 0.6 m away, the overhead and front metal framing, wooden blocking board, and recessed metal box sit within arm's reach at about 0.4 to 1.0 m, a power tool and fastener boxes rest on a lower horizontal track about 0.8 to 1.0 m below and in front of the wearer, and the deck floor with a white box and railing lies 1.5 to 3.0 m below and to the right. Across the five frames, the camera tilts slightly downward and right between frames 1 and 2 before steadying, while the right hand moves the clamp from the left stud in frame 1 to the right side of the wooden board in frame 2, pulls back to ~0.4 m in frames 3 and 4 where the left hand enters at the bottom center, and reaches up in frame 5 as both hands touch the board ~0.5 m away. The map clarifies the continuous 3D recession of the stud bays, the recessed depth of the metal housing behind the wooden board, and the sharp drop-off past the right wall edge to the deck below, which are harder to judge in the cluttered RGB image. However, the map is unreliable on the outdoor background beyond the deck railing (>10 m away), which is rendered completely black, and at the top-left of frames 1 to 4 where overexposure flattens the depth gradient across the studs and drywall.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map is extremely sparse and fails to capture the spatial layout of the metal-stud framing, deck, and tools, detecting only a few isolated regions across the five frames while no other people are present. It correctly segments the camera wearer's right forearm entering from the bottom right in frames 1, 4, and 5 as 'person' (at ~0.2 to 0.5 m distance, partially out of view below the frame edge), while completely missing the arm in frames 2 and 3. All other masks are severe misclassifications of objects within arm's reach (~0.4 to 0.8 m above and in front of the wearer): the wooden blocking board in frame 1 is labeled 'bed', the recessed metal box above the board in frames 4 and 5 is labeled 'tv', and the wearer's gloved left hand entering at the bottom center of frame 4 (about 0.15 m left of the right hand) is labeled 'cat'. Aside from isolating the sharp 2D boundary of the right forearm against the busy metallic background in frames 1, 4, and 5 and showing the upward reach of the right arm in frame 5, this map adds almost no spatial information beyond the RGB strip. It is highly unreliable due to hallucinated indoor object classes and complete omissions of the framing structure, C-clamp, and background deck.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across the five-frame strip, confirming that no other people are facing or looking toward the camera wearer, but failing to track the camera wearer's visible arms and hands in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5. Only in frame 3 does a small yellow body-skeleton fragment appear at the bottom center, roughly 0.3 to 0.5 m in front of and below the camera wearer's viewpoint, where the gloved right hand holds the C-clamp near the lower metal track. This isolated skeleton fragment hallucinates a miniature torso and limb structure aligned with the angled jaws and handles of the C-clamp and gloved fingers rather than accurately mapping the wearer's arm joints or magenta hand keypoints. Consequently, the pose map fails to show the movement of the right arm across the framing from left to right and the entry of the left arm in frames 4 and 5 as both hands reach the wooden board ~0.5 m away. It provides no reliable spatial detail beyond the RGB image and is entirely unreliable for tracking egocentric hand and arm articulation in this scene.
